newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CARDIFF AND BRIVE REACH EUROPEAN CUP QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CARDIFF AND BRIVE REACH EUROPEAN CUP QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Cardiff overcame atrocious weather in South Wales on Sunday to cruise past Milan 41-19 and reach the European Cup quarter-finals.
Cardiff scored four tries on a rain-sodden Arms Park pitch. They now top pool D of the 20-team competition after winning three of their four first round matches.
The Welsh side face either England's Bath, France's Dax or neighbours Pontypridd in the next round.
"I saw Dax play Bath yesterday, and was very impressed by them," Cardiff coach Terry Holmes said.
"It's going to be a hard job for Pontypridd to win there next weekend but I hope a couple of the other Welsh sides can follow us into the knock-out stages and help fly the flag."
Cardiff will be joined in the last eight by French side Brive, whose 23-10 pool C home win over Harlequins was capped by a brilliant injury time try from centre Sebastien Carrat.
"Brive deserved their victory," said France flanker Laurent Cabannes, who joined the London side this year. "They were better organised and more aggressive."
In the day's other match Italian club Treviso plundered seven tries in their 43-23 defeat of Edinburgh in Scotland to keep alive their outside chance of qualification from pool A.
